articles.title: Aaron Judge's Final Box Score Stats & Highlights in Yankees Return After 3-Month Injury Absence
articles.summary: Aaron Judge made his return to the New York Yankees' lineup during the team's matchup with the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Aaron Judge made his return to the New York Yankees' lineup during the team's matchup with the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday night.

Judge appeared in a game for the first time since May 31, as he was sidelined for just over three months due to a stress fracture of the first rib on his right side.

He played six innings before he was replaced by Heliot Ramos as New York eases him back into action.

It was a quiet night for Judge, as he went hitless in his three at-bats while striking out twice.

Still, the three-time American League MVP received a standing ovation from the fans at Yankee Stadium during his first plate appearance of the game.

Judge's early exit wasn't a surprise, as Yankees manager Aaron Boone confirmed that was the plan heading into the game.

"I'm going to be mindful of that, especially this first week," Boone said earlier on Tuesday, per ESPN's Jorge Castillo . "We'll adjust each night and what we see, but we want to build him up smartly."

It isn't too concerning that Judge wasn't able to look like his former self right away, although New York will be hoping that he gradually gets back on track with the postseason coming up.

The Yankees currently hold the No. 2 spot in the AL East standings with an 81-62 record, but they're just four games back from the Tampa Bay Rays for the division lead. They also own the top AL Wild Card spot.

As New York looks to make a deep postseason run, Judge's presence in its batting order will be crucial moving forward.

After earning his second consecutive AL MVP honor last season, he racked up 10 doubles, 17 home runs and 38 RBI while posting a .907 OPS in his first 59 games this year.

articles.title: Aaron Judge returns from months-long rib injury in Yankees' win over Rockies
articles.summary: Judge played just six innings and struck out twice in New York's 5-3 win on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Aaron Judge made his long-awaited return to Yankee Stadium on Tuesday.

Judge returned to the Yankees ' lineup for their 5-3 win over the Colorado Rockies in New York. It marked his first game back with the team after missing the past three months due to a stress fracture in his rib.

Judge received a big standing ovation from Yankees fans when he stepped into the box for the first time. He then struck out.

Judge struggled the rest of the way, too. He struck out again and then flied out to go 0-for-3 before he was pulled after six innings. He didn't get a chance to field a ball in right.

Judge's replacement, Heliot Ramos , drilled a three-run homer in the eighth to help power the Yankees to the victory.

Judge had most recently played on May 31 against the Athletics , and he has been slowly recovering from the stress fracture since then. Yankees manager Aaron Boone said last week that Judge was progressing well and building up his workload, and he opted to skip a minor-league rehab assignment. Judge joined the Yankees for their series against the Los Angeles Angels and San Diego Padres in California last week while continuing the recovery process.

On Monday, Judge took live batting practice at Yankee Stadium before he was activated , and then he made the trip over to the US Open in Queens to watch Coco Gauff in her match vs. Iva Jović.

Judge, 34, entered Tuesday with 17 home runs and 38 RBI this season. He holds a career-worst .248 batting average, but Tuesday was just his 60th game of the year.

"Having that guy setting the tone at the top of the lineup, we've missed that most of the season," catcher Austin Wells said last weekend before Judge's return, via The Athletic . "To have him come back at the most pivotal time of the year, I don't think there's anyone that can add the value that he will when he's back."

The Yankees sit at 82-62 after Tuesday's win, which has them in second in the AL East. They lead the American League wild-card race and seem well on their way to a third straight postseason trip.

Even though Judge didn't have the best outing, he's back on the field again with plenty of time to go before the playoffs. That's a start.

articles.summary: Aaron Judge went 0-for-3 with two strikeouts in his long-awaited Yankees return, but Heliot Ramos launched a three-run homer to steal the show.
articles.body: New York Yankees fans spent the last three months convincing themselves that Aaron Judge riding in like the White Knight was going to fix every single problem in the Bronx. Well, the Captain finally returned Tuesday night against the Colorado Rockies and dropped a total egg. Nobody expected a three-homer spectacle after 100 days on the shelf. But going 0-for-3 with two ugly, clueless strikeouts wasn't the heroic homecoming Bronx fans paid to see. He struck out swinging in his first turn, flied out in his second and then fanned looking in his third. To cap off the wildly underwhelming reboot, manager Aaron Boone pulled him after just six defensive innings. Ironically, the game-changing power surge didn't come from Number 99 at all. Judge's replacement provided the actual juice. With the Yankees trailing the Tampa Bay Rays in a tight AL East race, Judge insisted on jumping straight back into big-league action. articles.title: Elly De La Cruz Makes History with 105.3 MPH Throw to Stop Inside-the-Park HR in Reds vs. Dodgers
articles.summary: It appeared as if Los Angeles Dodgers right fielder Teoscar Hernández was going to have an inside-the-park home run during Tuesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds.
articles.body:
It appeared as if Los Angeles Dodgers right fielder Teoscar Hernández was going to have an inside-the-park home run during Tuesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds.

And then Elly De La Cruz unleashed a throw fast enough to make most roller coasters blush.

The Cincinnati Reds shortstop took the relay throw from the outfield and unleashed a 105.3 mph throw to the plate. By the time it arrived, tagging Hernández out was the easy part for catcher Jose Trevino.

For context, Andrew Destin of the Associated Press reported last season that Pittsburgh Pirates outfielder Oneil Cruz threw out J.P. Crawford of the Seattle Mariners at the plate with a 105.2 mph throw.

It was the second-fastest thrown ball for an outfield assist since Statcast began tracking such totals in 2015. Aaron Hicks of the New York Yankees threw one 105.5 mph during the 2016 campaign.

He has also been dominant at the plate of late and entered Tuesday's game with a .500/.556/.917 slash line, three home runs and seven RBI in six September games.

While the Reds are on the outside of the National League playoff picture looking, De La Cruz has been quite the bright spot. And he provided one of the highlights of the season to prevent a run Tuesday.

articles.title: Aaron Judge Reacts to Yankees Return, Standing Ovation After 3-Month Injury Absence
articles.summary: New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge told reporters that it "felt great" to make his return to the team during a 5-3 win over the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday.
articles.body:
New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge told reporters that it "felt great" to make his return to the team during a 5-3 win over the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday.

Judge went 0-for-3 with a pair of strikeouts in the contest.

He was replaced by Heliot Ramos after the sixth inning, as Yankees manager Aaron Boone chose to be cautious with Judge's playing time after he missed over three months due to a rib injury .

"I feel great, I played half a game so I don't know what to say about that," Judge said during his press conference.

"I respect Boonie so whatever he says I'm gonna do, but not happy about it," he added. "But, that's where my guy [Heliot] Ramos came in and picked me up and hit a nice little three-run homer there to put the game out so we can be comfortable going into the last inning. But yeah, not too happy about it."

Ramos hit a three-run home run for New York in the bottom of the eighth inning.

As for Judge, he also gave his thoughts on returning to game shape while simultaneously suiting up for the Bronx Bombers down the stretch of the regular season.

"I get paid to do this, so I gotta go do it," Judge explained. "That's the end of it. I get paid to go out there and give my best to the New York Yankees and these fans. So, you get paid to win games so you gotta keep going out there and winning games."

The three-time American League MVP discussed his recovery process as well, revealing that he wanted to come back months earlier than he eventually did.

"I wanted to come back a couple months ago, but I'm not a trainer, so I gotta check whatever boxes they got," Judge told reporters. "A box that they wanted me to check was live hitting so I said, 'Perfect, we'll do that on the off day so I can play.'"

Judge also reacted to the standing ovation that he received from the crowd at Yankee Stadium in the bottom of the first inning.

"It was great," he said. "It reminded me a little bit of in '22, going for 62. They were all on their feet, but it was kind of quiet as he was pitching. I didn't like that that much. But standing 'O,' going up there was great. That's why they're the best fans in the world, so I was just trying to put a show on for them and come out with a win."

The Yankees improved to 82-62 with the victory, clinching their 34th consecutive season with a winning record.

"We're the Yankees, we're gonna win," Judge told reporters. "That's a great streak but everybody in this room is worried about championships."

New York holds the top AL Wild Card spot and sits four games back from the Tampa Bay Rays for the AL East lead with 18 regular-season contests remaining.

articles.title: Ranking the 10 Most Underrated Yankees of All Time
articles.summary: It's not easy to be underrated playing for the New York Yankees.
articles.body:
It's not easy to be underrated playing for the New York Yankees.

More often than not, a Yankees player is going to be overrated before he's underrated. It just comes with the territory.

However, from championship drought standouts to short-peak stars, there are a handful of Yankees players who don't get the recognition they deserve. They make up our list of the 10 most underrated Yankees of all time.

It's worth noting that there is a difference between underrated and simply forgotten. Expect this list to skew heavily toward more recent players, though there are a handful of vintage throwbacks.

Tenure: 2005-2009 Stats: 104 GS, 55-26, 4.16 ERA, 310 K, 670.2 IP WAR: 14.0

Chien-Ming Wang debuted as the Yankees dynasty was wrapping up. His peak concluded before they won their next World Series in 2009, leaving him as something of a tweener lost to time. A severe right foot injury that he suffered while running the bases derailed his career at the age of 28.

Wang's prime lasted only two years before his 2008 injury.

2006: 33 GS, 19-6, 3.63 ERA, 218.0 IP, 6.0 WAR 2007: 30 GS, 19-7, 3.70 ERA, 199.1 IP, 5.0 WAR

His 2006 season was good for a runner-up finish in AL Cy Young balloting, and while he spent those two years sharing the rotation with Roger Clemens, Mike Mussina, Randy Johnson, Andy Pettitte and others, he was the best arm on the staff.

Tenure: 1998-2001 Stats: 540 G, 96 OPS+, .267/.331/.428, 173 XBH (65 HR) WAR: 8.3

After seven seasons with the Oakland Athletics, Scott Brosius was traded to the Yankees in exchange for left-hander Kenny Rogers ahead of the 1998 season. He then promptly won three straight World Series titles as the team's primary third baseman. He won the 1998 World Series MVP and hit a dramatic game-tying home run with two outs in the bottom of the ninth in Game 5 of the 2001 Fall Classic.

The huge postseason resume is what fans remember, but he was more than just an October standout. In 1998, his 5.3 WAR was the third-highest mark for one of the greatest teams in MLB history, behind only Derek Jeter and Paul O'Neill. He also won a Gold Glove the following year, showcasing his two-way value.

Playoff legend? Absolutely, but he was also a well-rounded contributor before the calendar flipped to October.

Tenure: 2015-2019 Stats: 660 G, 102 OPS+, .269/.313/.446, 228 XBH (97 HR) WAR: 14.8

Hall of Famer Derek Jeter played his final MLB season in 2014. With no clear in-house replacement at shortstop in place, Didi Gregorius was acquired from Arizona in a three-team deal with the D-backs and Tigers. He spent five seasons as the team's primary shortstop before passing the torch to Gleyber Torres in 2020, earning MVP votes twice along the way.

Given impossible shoes to fill, Gregorius ultimately did a pretty stellar job. His 14.5 WAR trailed only Francisco Lindor (22.2), Andrelton Simmons (22.1), Carlos Correa (21.3), Xander Bogaerts (15.2) and Brandon Crawford (15.0) among all shortstops from 2015-18.

In the years since his departure, the Yankees have shuffled through Gleyber Torres, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Anthony Volpe and now George Lombard Jr. at the position, with no one from that group providing a comparable sustained run.

Tenure: 1979-1990 Stats: 522 G, 76 GS, 74-61, 224 SV, 3.11 ERA, 1,136.2 IP WAR: 22.9

After three seasons as a staple in the Yankees rotation, including 1981 AL Rookie of the Year and a 1983 no-hitter, Dave Righetti was moved to the bullpen to replace Goose Gossage in the closer's role. It proved to be a terrific fit. In 1986, he set the single-season saves record at the time with 46. He still ranks as one of the most successful relievers in franchise history.

Pitchers often move to the bullpen after flaming out in a starting role or suffering an injury, but Righetti did it just as he was entering his prime and coming off a fantastic 1983 season.

1983: 31 GS, 14-8, 3.44 ERA, 169 K, 217.0 IP, 3.6 WAR 1984: 64 G, 31 SV, 2.34 ERA, 90 K, 96.1 IP, 3.3 WAR

It's not a move many players in today's game would accept, but one he made seamlessly. His 224 saves in an era before that became a more prominent stat still rank second in franchise history.

Tenure: 1987-1992, 2000 Stats: 648 G, 107 OPS+, .278/.331/.411, 180 XBH (57 HR), 151 SB WAR: 13.2

The Yankees signed Roberto Kelly out of Panama as a teenager in 1982. By 1989, he was the team's starting center fielder. During a four-year run in that role, he hit .281/.334/.415 for a 109 OPS+ while averaging 14 home runs, 34 steals and 3.2 WAR, earning an All-Star selection in 1992.

A single All-Star selection might not sound significant until you realize how rare it is for a homegrown Yankees outfielder to earn a spot in the Midsummer Classic. In the last 50 years, here is the entire list of those who accomplished it:

Aaron Judge (8) Bernie Williams (5) Brett Gardner (1) Roberto Kelly (1)

For many Yankees fans, his enduring legacy is that he went the other way in the deal to acquire fan favorite Paul O'Neill from Cincinnati, but he was a terrific player himself during his time in the Bronx.

Tenure: 1993-1996 Stats: 94 GS, 48-23, 3.68 ERA, 400 K, 604.1 IP WAR: 13.5

After whiffing in their pursuit of Greg Maddux and Doug Drabek prior to the 1993 season, the Yankees inked Jimmy Key to a four-year, $17 million deal. The 32-year-old immediately became the ace of the staff. In his final appearance in a Yankees uniform, he was the winning pitcher in Game 6 of the 1996 World Series.

While his role on the 1996 championship team provided his most memorable moments in New York, Key was legitimately one of the best pitchers in baseball during his first two seasons in the Bronx.

1993: 34 GS, 18-6, 3.00 ERA, 236.2 IP, 6.3 WAR, 4th in AL Cy Young 1994: 25 GS, 17-4, 3.27 ERA, 168.0 IP, 4.4 WAR, 2nd in AL Cy Young

If the players' strike hadn't brought the 1994 season to a premature end, he might have been a 20-game winner and pushed David Cone for Cy Young honors. Even with an injury-plagued 1995 season, he stands as one of the best free-agent signings in franchise history.

Tenure: 1951-1960 Stats: 1,336 G, 111 OPS+, .276/.356/.410, 350 XBH (112 HR) WAR: 40.9

A six-time All-Star and the 1951 AL Rookie of the Year, Gil McDougald spent his entire career in pinstripes. In an era of set positions, he provided valuable versatility with extensive action at second base, shortstop and third base. He won five rings and played in eight World Series over a 10-year career.

When you can count Mickey Mantle, Joe DiMaggio, Yogi Berra, Whitey Ford and Phil Rizzuto among your teammates, it's not hard to see why McDougald often gets lost in the shuffle, but he was a legitimate impact player with at least 3 WAR in nine of his 10 years in the big leagues.

To put his 40.9 WAR into context, Hall of Famer Bill Mazeroski tallied 36.5 WAR while playing seven more seasons in the majors.

Tenure: 1996-2002, 2005 Stats: 278 G, 57 GS, 54-34, 16 SV, 4.10 ERA, 699.2 IP WAR: 11.6

Signed by the Yankees out of Panama, Ramiro Mendoza debuted with an ugly 6.78 ERA in 11 starts during the team's 1996 World Series season. He quickly settled into a versatile swingman role in the years that followed. Mendoza was a key arm on the 1998 and 1999 World Series teams.

The 1998 season is the perfect snapshot of why Mendoza was such a valuable Swiss Army knife on the Yankees staff.

41 G, 14 GS, 10-2, 1 SV, 3.25 ERA, 130.1 IP

He threw a five-hit shutout on May 10, logging a 2.2-inning save on July 10. He also pitched scoreless sixth, seventh and eighth innings in Game 6 of the ALCS on Oct. 13. Any role, any time, he was ready to take the ball.

Tenure: 1992-1995, 1997 Stats: 426 G, 134 OPS+, .285/.377/.504, 155 XBH (72 HR) WAR: 12.8

Mike Stanley was 29 years old with six forgettable seasons as a part-time player with the Texas Rangers when he joined the Yankees on a minor league deal. After serving as the backup to Matt Nokes in 1992, he took over as the team's primary catcher and won a Silver Slugger and made an All-Star team during a standout three-year stretch.

From 1993-95, Stanley posted a 136 OPS+ while averaging 20 home runs and 75 RBI and logging at least 3 WAR each season. Here's a full list of every Yankees catcher with three or more 3-WAR seasons:

Yogi Berra (10) Bill Dickey (9) Thurman Munson (9) Jorge Posada (8) Elston Howard (5) Gary Sánchez (3) Mike Stanley (3)

Ask the average Yankees fan that trivia question, and there's a good chance Stanley is the one name they can't pull.

Tenure: 1964-1974 Stats: 356 GS, 164-139, 2.97 ERA, 2,661.1 IP WAR: 40.7

Mel Stottlemyre was a five-time All-Star over an 11-year career spent entirely with the Yankees, as he shows up all over the franchise's all-time leaderboard. He ranks inside the top 10 in pitching WAR (40.7, 8th), wins (164, 7th), strikeouts (1,257, 8th), innings pitched (2,661.1, 4th), complete games (152, 8th) and shutouts (40, 2nd). He later served as the team's pitching coach from 1996-2005, which is probably how most modern Yankees fans remember him.

In Stottlemyre's rookie season in 1964, the Yankees lost the World Series in seven games. They would not return to the Fall Classic until 1976, two years after he retired. That is why he's so underrated, in a nutshell.

In a franchise loaded with postseason heroes, his playoff resume consisted of three starts as a 22-year-old in the 1964 World Series. He went 1-1 with a 3.15 ERA in 20 innings. He was the bridge between Whitey Ford and Ron Guidry, but his contributions are often overlooked as a result.

articles.title: Tier Rankings For MLB's 50 Best Hitters of 2026 Season
articles.summary: Who have been the 50 best MLB hitters in 2026? We've broken it down into eight tiers to try to get to that answer.
articles.body:
Who have been the 50 best MLB hitters in 2026? We've broken it down into eight tiers to try to get to that answer.

Evaluations were based not only on hitting but also on the ability to draw walks for this list. Stolen bases and fielding were not considered. It's all about what you do at the plate.

With that acknowledged, here are our tier rankings for MLB's 50 best hitters of the 2026 season starting with Tier 8.

Who: Players who haven't had a full elite season, either because of injuries or underperformance, but have been tremendous at their best

Stats: .274 BA, 23 HR, 56 RBI, 66 BB, .922 OPS

The Mets are about to be 0-for-2 in the Juan Soto Era in terms of playoff appearances, but it's not his fault. He was an All-Star for the second time in as many seasons in Flushing, and would probably have been looking at a second consecutive top-five finish in NL MVP voting if not for a pair of calf strains limiting him to 92 games.

Stats: .280 BA, 20 HR, 71 RBI, 55 BB, .794 OPS

It was a nightmarish start to the season for Fernando Tatis Jr., who didn't hit his first home run of the season until May 30. However, he's also the primary reason the Padres remain in the wild-card race. FanGraphs says he's third in WAR among all position players since the start of June.

Stats: .256 BA, 21 HR, 69 RBI, 79 BB, .879 OPS

A right thumb strain has ended Nick Kurtz's season prematurely, but make no mistake, the defending AL Rookie of the Year still looks likely to be one of the faces of the sport in the coming years. In 99 games this season, Kurtz homered 21 times, drove in 69 runs and drew 79 walks.

Stats: .250 BA, 24 HR, 81 RBI, 69 BB, .790 OPS

Alex Bregman got off to a slow start with the Cubs after joining Chicago on a five-year, $175 million contract in free agency this past winter. He's made up for lost time in a monster second half that's seen him post two three-homer games. Since the All-Star break, he's second only to his teammate Pete Crow-Armstrong in OPS.

Stats: .264 BA, 12 HR, 62 RBI, 56 BB, .756 OPS

Cody Bellinger missed nearly a month with a left hamstring strain, but other than that, it's been a very successful season after the former NL MVP returned to the Yankees on a five-year, $162.5 million deal in the offseason. Bellinger won the All-Star Game MVP and continues to be a force at Yankee Stadium, as he's posted a .924 OPS in home games this season.

Stats: .248 BA, 19 HR, 60 RBI, 45 BB, .812 OPS

A pair of hamstring strains has limited Kyle Stowers' availability in 2026, but he's been excellent when available, with 19 homers, 60 RBI, and 45 walks in just over 104 games. Stowers still has three years of arbitration until free agency, so he should be a building block for the Fish going forward.

Stats: .245 BA, 19 HR, 56 RBI, 53 BB, .810 OPS

It's been a very disappointing season for the A's, but Soderstrom has homered 19 times and posted an .810 OPS in 109 games. Unfortunately, he's now on the injured list with a left hip impingement for the second time this season.

Stats: .302 BA, 10 HR, 63 RBI, 32 BB, .778 OPS

Otto Lopez would have been in a higher tier at the season's midpoint, when he was an All-Star after hitting .334 in 95 games. He's still worth a mention here because of his first half, but he's struggled since, with a .225 batting average after the Midsummer Classic. Unsurprisingly, the Marlins have faded as he has.

Who: Excellent players who don't get enough attention nationally

Stats: .256 BA, 29 HR, 83 RBI, 54 BB, .803 OPS

The Pirates underwhelmed as a team, but Brandon Lowe has had a very nice season in Pittsburgh after being acquired in an offseason trade from the Tampa Bay Rays. He's homered 29 times and driven in 83 runs for the Buccos, which should set him up well for a multi-year deal in free agency this offseason.

Stats: .256 BA, 23 HR, 70 RBI, 64 BB, .799 OPS

Wilyer Abreu has been a key cog for a Red Sox team that's turned things around after a brutal start. In addition to his 23 homers, Abreu leads baseball with 34 doubles.

Stats: .293 BA, 15 HR, 75 RBI, 28 BB, .821 OPS

A change of scenery has done wonders for McCarthy, who has hit .293 with 29 doubles and 75 RBI in his first season with the Rockies after an offseason trade from the Diamondbacks. He has certainly benefited from playing his home games at Coors Field, where he has an .875 OPS. However, he's still been effective in road games, with a .741 OPS.

Stats: .275 BA, 18 HR, 62 RBI, 62 BB, .831 OPS

Riley Greene hasn't matched the 36 homers he hit a year ago, but he's still managed to get on base more consistently. The 62 walks he has in 2026 are just two away from tying a career high. His .365 on-base percentage is markedly better than the .313 OBP he had a year ago.

Stats: .283 BA, 22 HR, 104 RBI, 48 BB, .812 OPS

Alec Burleson won a Silver Slugger in 2025, and still seems to fly under the radar. It will be increasingly hard to overlook the left-handed slugger after his second consecutive season with an OPS north of .800 and his first with over 100 runs driven in.

Who: These are players 25 and younger who aren't going to win an MVP in 2026, but have been good enough to make you wonder whether they could someday.

Stats: .278 BA, 22 HR, 69 RBI, 50 BB, .807 OPS

Last year's NL Rookie of the Year has continued to emerge as one of the best hitters in the senior circuit regardless of position. A first-time All-Star, Baldwin did miss close to a month with an oblique strain, but he's been tremendous the rest of the season.

Stats: .280 BA, 23 HR, 66 RBI, 61 BB, .852 OPS

There hasn't been a ton of hype around him because the Reds have underperformed as a team, but Elly De La Cruz has probably put together his best overall offensive season in 2026. Interestingly, De La Cruz's hard-hit rate has gone up from 33.9 percent in 2025 to 46.9 percent in 2026.

Stats: .281 BA, 21 HR, 59 RBI, 39 BB, .810 OPS

Jackson Chourio is still only 22 years old, so he's probably just scratching the surface of his offensive potential, which should be scary for the rest of the league. If a .770 OPS last year felt a bit underwhelming, Chourio has taken a major step forward with an .810 OPS in 2026.

Stats: .291 BA, 24 HR, 80 RBI, 20 BB, .813 OPS

Michael Harris II disappointed in 2025, hitting .249 with a .678 OPS. The former NL Rookie of the Year has rebounded in a major way in 2026, to the point where it feels like a pretty bad oversight that he wasn't an All-Star.

Stats: .272 BA, 21 HR, 80 RBI, 45 BB, .797 OPS

As if the two-time defending World Series champions needed another stud, Andy Pages was an All-Star in 2026. Unfortunately, his regular season was halted (and possibly ended) by a left-hand fracture in late August. Nonetheless, he went from unplayable offensively last October to one of the most well-rounded players in the sport this season.

Stats: .271 BA, 14 HR, 59 RBI, 85 BB, .782 OPS

The Tigers are likely very happy with the eight-year, $150 million contract they gave to Kevin McGonigle just a couple of weeks into his MLB career. As a rookie, he was an All-Star.

Who: It might not have been the best season of their career, but these veteran stars padded their resumes with another tremendous campaign.

Stats: .249 BA, 26 HR, 68 RBI, 60 BB, .834 OPS

2026 is the fifth season in which Max Muncy has hit 25 or more homers. As hard as it may be to believe, he's now the all-time leader in home runs at Dodger Stadium. Even at age 36, Muncy shows no signs of slowing down.

Stats: .318 BA, 6 HR, 57 RBI, 28 BB, .780 OPS

While he hasn't hit for quite as high an average since being traded from the San Francisco Giants to the Phillies, Luis Arraez still has the highest batting average in baseball. If he holds on, this would be his fourth career batting title, and he's still only 29 years old.

Stats: .258 BA, 35 HR, 91 RBI, 66 BB, .856 OPS

If you thought Rafael Devers' contract looked bad early in the season, it now seems like the bargain it is. He leads baseball in doubles and has homered 35 or more times for the third time in his career. Devers will turn 30 in October, and he's put together a hell of a résumé already.

Stats: .240 BA, 19 HR, 61 RBI, 69 BB, .803 OPS

For the third consecutive season, Carroll leads baseball in triples. This would be his fourth year in a row with the most triples in the National League. Carroll hasn't hit for as much power as his 31 home runs last season, but he's still managed to hit for a ton of extra-base hits, as he's topped 30 doubles for the third time in four years.

Stats: .285 BA, 17 HR, 51 RBI, 59 BB, .817 OPS

Bobby Witt Jr. leads all American League players in WAR , which gives you an idea of how well-rounded he is. Offensively, this probably isn't Witt's best season, but it's still been very good, including a career high in walks.

Stats: .301 BA, 16 HR, 66 RBI, 64 BB, .838 OPS

Perhaps he's not at the height of his powers anymore, but Freddie Freeman was still an All-Star this year, marking his 10th career selection to the Midsummer Classic. He's going to go down as one of the most consistent hitters in baseball history.

Who: These hitters aren't necessarily established stars, but their 2026 seasons are worthy of acknowledgment.

Stats: .270 BA, 24 HR, 78 RBI, 86 BB, .889 OPS

Stats: .284 BA, 28 HR, 88 RBI, 23 BB, .859 OPS

articles.title: Elly De La Cruz Makes History with 102 MPH Throw to Stop Inside-the-Park HR in Reds vs. Dodgers
articles.summary: It appeared as if Los Angeles Dodgers right fielder Teoscar Hernández was going to have an inside-the-park home run during Tuesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds.
articles.body:
It appeared as if Los Angeles Dodgers right fielder Teoscar Hernández was going to have an inside-the-park home run during Tuesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds.

And then Elly De La Cruz unleashed a throw fast enough to make most roller coasters blush.

The Cincinnati Reds shortstop took the relay throw from the outfield and unleashed a heater to the plate. By the time it arrived, tagging Hernández out was the easy part for catcher Jose Trevino.

While the throw was initially logged at 105.3 mph, it was later updated to 102 mph:

For context, Andrew Destin of the Associated Press reported last season that Pittsburgh Pirates outfielder Oneil Cruz threw out J.P. Crawford of the Seattle Mariners at the plate with a 105.2 mph throw.

It was the second-fastest thrown ball for an outfield assist since Statcast began tracking such totals in 2015. Aaron Hicks of the New York Yankees threw one 105.5 mph during the 2016 campaign.

Per MLB's Sarah Langs , De La Cruz's 102 mph throw is the fastest assist by an infielder since 2015, surpassing the 99.8 mph throw he previously made.

Langs noted that only 10 outfielder assists have topped 102 mph during that span. So, De La Cruz is in excellent company.

He has also been dominant at the plate of late and entered Tuesday's game with a .500/.556/.917 slash line, three home runs and seven RBI in six September games.

While the Reds are on the outside of the National League playoff picture looking, De La Cruz has been quite the bright spot. And he provided one of the highlights of the season to prevent a run Tuesday.

articles.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Injury Update, Latest News on Return Timeline to Yankees Amid Anthony Volpe Buzz
articles.summary: The New York Yankees will have to continue their bid to hold on to the top AL Wild Card spot at least for now without second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees will have to continue their bid to hold on to the top AL Wild Card spot at least for now without second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr.

Chisholm is being placed on the 10-day injured list with a right thumb sprain that will keep him from baseball activities for seven to 10 days, manager Aaron Boone said Wednesday.

Boone said he did not yet know who would replace Chisholm on the roster but would be comfortable playing Anthony Volpe at second base, per Greg Joyce of the New York Post .

Chisholm suffered the injury while sliding into second base during Tuesday night's win over the visiting Colorado Rockies, per MLB.com .

The news comes after the Yankees began transitioning Anthony Volpe from shortstop to second and third base in Triple-A action last month.

The slide took place in Tuesday's eighth inning. Chisholm was replaced by José Cabellero for the top of the ninth.

Volpe, who played the entirety of his MLB career at shortstop and won a Gold Glove at the position during his rookie 2023 season, was demoted Aug. 4 after struggling early in the 2026 campaign.

He has since found success with Scranton/Wilke-Barre RailRiders, where he has batted .295 with ten home runs and seven doubles in 27 games while regularly playing at second base.

"I know he's been a complete pro and completely got after it down there in everything they've thrown at him... he's obviously swung the bat incredibly well," Boone said Wednesday about Volpe. "That's not an easy thing to do when you've been in the big leagues, and you've been the guy in the big leagues, and you've got to go back."

The Yankees went into Wednesday's matchup against the Rockies with Cabellero at second base.

The departure of Chisholm, who is batting .232 with 19 home runs this season, marks the latest injury absence from a Yankees lineup that just got back Aaron Judge after three months on the injured list.

Judge made his comeback Tuesday against the Rockies, but was pulled by Boone after six innings. Boone said there was a possibility Judge would be limited again in his second game against the Rockies, but that he also might "push a little more" in Wednesday's matchup.

articles.title: Yankees add Jazz Chisholm Jr. to IL with sprained right thumb
articles.summary: Chisholm will be shut down from baseball activities for 7 to 10 days.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees are adding second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. to the injured list due to a sprained right thumb, per manager Aaron Boone .

Chisholm will be shut down from baseball activities for seven to 10 days, leaving it unclear how long his stay on the IL will be.

The second baseman has played in 134 games this season. He is slashing .232/.312/.403 with 19 home runs and 55 RBI. If Chisholm is unable to return during the regular season, this would be the lowest batting average of his career for seasons in which he played in at least 22 games.

One of the lone bright spots for Chisholm's 2026 campaign is that he has tied a career high with 40 stolen bases. There was a time when he said his goal was a 40/40 season, and it seemed after his 31 home runs last year that he may have a decent shot at the feat, but barring an extreme power surge upon his return, he figures to fall well short this season.

Boone did not know who would be replacing Chisholm, but at least in the immediate short term, it will be Jose Caballero playing second base Wednesday night against the Colorado Rockies .

One of the options from New York 's minor league system is Anthony Volpe . The middle infielder had struggled in the bigs with New York both in the field and at the plate.

Volpe was sent down in favor of George Lombard Jr., but the move sparked something in the young player. Volpe has played in 37 games with the team's Triple-A affiliate and is batting .264 with 11 home runs. Over 56 games with the Yankees earlier in the season, the infielder was hitting .240 and had only one home run.

New York heads into Wednesday with an 82-62 record, four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East race. The Yankees currently comfortably hold the AL's No. 1 Wild Card spot with a nine-game spread between them and the team falling out of the playoff picture.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Dodgers Star's Timeline Ahead of 2026 MLB Playoffs
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani will reportedly be out of the lineup once again when the Los Angeles Dodgers face the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Shohei Ohtani will reportedly be out of the lineup once again when the Los Angeles Dodgers face the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday.

The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya reported the slugger will not play for the sixth time in seven games due to knee, biceps and neck injuries. This is a change from the Dodgers' previous plans of playing him Wednesday after he had the day off Tuesday.

"Talking to the training staff, it's more of the thought of, 'Let's build him up slowly,'" Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday.

The two-way star hasn't pitched since July 3 but had been playing designated hitter on a consistent basis until these recent issues. Monday's win over the Reds was the only time he's been in the lineup since Sept. 2.

He went 0-for-3 with a walk and two strikeouts in that one.

When healthy, the four-time MVP remains one of the best players in baseball even when he isn't pitching. He has been largely excellent at the plate this season and is slashing .277/.380/.522 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI and 11 stolen bases.

His overall presence is a major reason the Dodgers are back-to-back World Series champions, and they surely have their eye on October with the latest caution.

Where Los Angeles will be come October remains to be seen, as it is 1.5 games behind the Milwaukee Brewers in the race for the No. 1 seed in the National League and three games ahead of the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed.

Fortunately for the Dodgers, they have played well of late even without Ohtani and enter Wednesday's contest on a six-game winning streak.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani remains out for Dodgers after return from 4-game absence amid struggles, lingering injuries
articles.summary: The Dodgers expected Shohei Ohtani to return to the lineup on Wednesday after he missed Tuesday's contest, but they reversed course and kept him out instead.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers ' star did not play in the team's 3-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Tuesday night, one day after he returned from a four-game absence due to several lingering injuries.

Ohtani missed Tuesday's game so that the team can "build him up slowly," manager Dave Roberts said pregame, via the California Post's Jack Harris .

Roberts said after Tuesday's contest that Ohtani would be back in the lineup on Wednesday for their series finale with the Reds. Yet on Wednesday afternoon, the Dodgers reversed course and kept Ohtani out of the lineup. That marked his sixth absence in a seven-game stretch.

Roberts said before Wednesday's game that Ohtani simply hasn't "totally recovered" from Monday's game, and that there was a swing that night that "didn't feel great."

Before Monday, Ohtani missed four games while recovering from left biceps, left knee and neck issues. The reigning National League MVP struck out four times in a game last week and has noticeably struggled lately.

After Monday's game, Ohtani told reporters through an interpreter that he is still dealing with the lingering injuries and that the main concerns are his arm and his knee.

"I've been training a little bit more, doing just supplementary things to be able to make sure that I'm in a good place. I hope to continue to do that to make sure that I'm up to shape," Ohtani said, via The Athletic . "I should have enough experience to be able to address any kinks or injuries or anything like that with the swing. I'm going to use this as an opportunity to add on to the experience that I've had previously and be able to address it regardless."

In Monday's 6-3 win over the Reds , Ohtani struck out twice and walked once. He did not record a hit. Ohtani had just a .241/.322/.422 slash line in August, too; all of those numbers are far below his marks from the previous four months of the season.

Amid his struggles, both Ohtani and the Dodgers have said he almost certainly won't pitch again in 2026. Ohtani told reporters Monday that he would be "focusing on hitting moving forward," something he said was "disappointing."

He has not pitched since July 3, largely due to the left knee injury. In 14 starts this season, he has a 1.79 ERA and an 8-2 record.

With Ohtani out, the Dodgers put Tommy Edman in the leadoff spot and moved Freddie Freeman into the designated hitter role for Tuesday. Will Smith opened the game with a home run, and the Dodgers pulled ahead for good after an RBI single from Teoscar Hernandez in the fifth.

It doesn't sound like Ohtani will be placed on the injured list. But given that he's still a two-way player, he would have to stay there for a minimum of 15 days should the Dodgers go that route. That would put his return right up against the end of the regular season, leaving him little time to ramp up before the playoffs.

Regardless of what happens, Ohtani's status is very much up in the air.

"I think we got through tonight," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said after Monday's game. "For me, I'll just see how he feels tomorrow."

Even with Ohtani's health issues, the Dodgers hold a double-digit lead in the NL West and sit at 88-57 after Tuesday's win. They've won six straight, too.

But if Ohtani is out for any significant stretch of time or his injuries linger into the postseason, the Dodgers' quest for a third straight World Series title will undoubtedly be much more difficult.

Ohtani's postseason eligibility, Roberts said, is the focus.

"It's not about just tonight ... It's about, 'What can we do to get him to be optimum as we get into the postseason?'" Roberts said, via The Athletic's Katie Woo . "I think that a day here or there is not the worst thing to make sure that his body overall feels as close to 100% as possible."

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani injury saga: What's the latest, and where do the Dodgers go from here?
articles.summary: Ohtani is 'focusing on hitting moving forward,' which raises an entirely new series of questions involving his season and L.A.'s push for a third straight ch...
articles.body:
When Shohei Ohtani arrived stateside in 2018 after a legendary, half-decade run as a two-way player in Japan's NPB, his ambition of hitting and pitching simultaneously in MLB invited two central questions.

The first involved his raw ability: Was Ohtani good enough to do both at the highest level the sport has to offer? Four unanimous MVP awards and a treasure trove of previously unfathomable on-field achievements later, Ohtani has answered that question with an emphatic yes.

The second question centered on a more practical concern: Could his body handle the physical toll of regularly pitching and hitting in the major leagues? The answer to that question, for the most part, has been no.

While Ohtani has amassed more than enough playing time to rack up individual accolades and a couple of championships, it's impossible to ignore how often his superhuman pursuits have been interrupted by the sobering reality of being human. Just twice — in 2021 and 2022 — has Ohtani completed a full season of playing both ways fully healthy. Two elbow surgeries — one during his rookie season in 2018 and another at the conclusion of his final season as an Angel in 2023 — have limited his availability on the mound to varying degrees in every other year.

But this year, with Ohtani's second elbow procedure fading in the rearview mirror, there was hope that the singular superstar could sustain his full-fledged two-way responsibilities for the entirety of a campaign for a third time. He reminded us in October — much to the Milwaukee Brewers' dismay — what he could achieve at the peak of his powers. Entering his third season in Dodger blue, Ohtani seemed eager to deliver the goods across a full season in support of Los Angeles ' attempt to three-peat. His unparalleled ambition was perhaps best exemplified by the preseason whispers that he had his sights set on the Cy Young Award, a not-so-humble sidequest to his everyday mission as the Dodgers ' leadoff hitter.

For two months, Ohtani seemed on track to once again do the impossible. Across his first 10 starts, he posted a preposterous 0.74 ERA in 61 innings while striking out 67 batters and allowing just 30 hits. His OPS hovered around .900, a bit below the standard he'd set for himself but still among the best marks in the league. Ohtani's chances of keeping pace in a crowded NL Cy Young field were cloudy based on his limited workload relative to his competition, but in the early going, he was well on his way to a fifth MVP award in the past six seasons and somehow living up to the outlandish preseason expectations.

But then June brought the first of a series of physical setbacks that would derail not just Ohtani's Cy Young push but his MVP hopes as well.

It began in his 11th start of the season on June 10 in Pittsburgh . Ohtani surrendered a season-high four runs across 6 ⅔ innings while dealing with a blister on his right middle finger that he downplayed postgame . The more troubling sequence occurred the next day, when Ohtani experienced pain in his left knee on a stolen base attempt, enough to prompt Roberts to pinch-hit for him in the seventh inning of a one-run game. This was the same knee on which Ohtani required surgery toward the end of his second season with the Angels in 2019. No matter. After sitting out one game, Ohtani returned to the lineup the next day and hit a leadoff homer , quieting concerns that he'd suffered a significant injury.

But while Ohtani continued to mash through June (1.091 OPS), his effectiveness on the mound wavered, at least compared to his early-season excellence. The Rays tagged him for four runs on June 17. Minnesota scored three against him on June 24. Then, the day before his scheduled start against the A's on July 1, the Dodgers announced that Ohtani would instead start a couple days later against the Padres. He delivered a quality start against San Diego , throwing a season-high 110 pitches, but was pinch-hit for later in the game after he felt some tightness in his right biceps. When his next turn through the Dodgers' rotation arrived, Ohtani was scratched. That announcement came with the news that Ohtani would skip the All-Star Game in Philadelphia , an event he headlined the previous five seasons.

"The goal is to be able to throw according to a regular schedule [in the second half]," Ohtani said through interpreter Will Ireton after his scratched outing. "Although I could've started, it would've still been pushing the envelope a little bit."

The plan then was for Ohtani to get treatment on his left knee and use the break to rest, with hopes of working toward a return to the mound. "My every intention is to use the off days to make sure I'm in a good place to be able to be in the rotation," he said.

But when his first scheduled start of the second half arrived the following week, Ohtani was scratched again, with Roberts declaring a more prolonged pause in his pitching on July 19 .

At that point, it was difficult to decipher whether the delays in Ohtani's return to the mound were more reflective of his physical ailments or the Dodgers' preference to be patient given their circumstances. Perhaps the aggressive acquisition of Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline was an exorbitant insurance policy in case Ohtani's availability to pitch was indeed in jeopardy.

Or maybe the Dodgers were just doing what they always do, supercharging their roster when the opportunity arose, with hopes that Skubal and Ohtani could both star on their pitching staff come October. Plus, with proven October titan Yoshinobu Yamamoto cruising and Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow close to coming off the injured list, the Dodgers had no reason to rush Ohtani back if he wasn't completely ready.

With a comfortable lead atop the NL West , optimism remained that Ohtani had enough time to ramp back up to two-way status before the postseason. He threw a 30-pitch live bullpen session on Aug. 22 , setting the stage for a possible return to action in Detroit the following week. But after Ohtani threw an abbreviated bullpen at Comerica Park on Aug. 28, Roberts ruled out the possibility of him pitching that Sunday as previously suggested, opting to reassess matters upon returning to Los Angeles.

That weekend in Detroit, Roberts was not subtle in communicating the organization's preference to prioritize getting Ohtani back on track with the bat, rather than continuing to push through his ailments in hopes he could contribute on the mound.

"Obviously, where we're at right now with the pitching, the starting pitching certainly being a strength, his value offensively is hugely important," Roberts said. "And so we can't compromise that in any fashion. So if throwing potentially cuts into that, that's not worth the squeeze. [We're] very bullish on making sure we don't compromise the hitting."

By then, however, the hitting already appeared compromised.

As Ohtani the pitcher worked on his buildup behind the scenes, Ohtani the slugger seemed to become less dangerous. After homering twice against the Cubs on Aug. 5, Ohtani went deep only four more times over 22 games to finish the month, and three of those came at Coors Field. His .795 OPS in August wasn't so bad by mere mortal standards, but it was his worst mark in a calendar month since April 2022 (.722). And while Ohtani was far from the biggest culprit, his unusual inconsistency atop L.A.'s lineup was a glaring shortcoming amid an offense slumping across the board. The Dodgers hit .241/.311/.378 in August, amounting to a .689 OPS that ranked 21st in MLB.

Ohtani's struggles with the bat worsened as the month came to a close. He went 1-for-13 with five strikeouts in Detroit. Back home against the Cardinals, he went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts on Sept. 2 — his first four-strikeout showing since NLDS Game 1 against the Phillies last fall. With that, Roberts had seen enough ; Ohtani needed to sit, to reset, to recuperate. A trip to the injured list was avoided (because of his status as a two-way player, Ohtani would need to be placed on the 15-day IL rather than the 10-day like most position players), but Ohtani sat out the next four games , marking an unprecedented pause in his time with the Dodgers.

He returned to the leadoff spot Monday against Cincinnati , but his 0-for-3 was hardly the headline. Speaking to reporters postgame for the first time since Aug. 17, Ohtani confirmed what Roberts had hinted at over the weekend: He is no longer working toward a return to pitching in 2026.

"Most likely, no," Ohtani said through Ireton. "I'm going to be focusing on hitting moving forward."

"I think the thing that I was more focused on was making sure that the pitching wouldn't cause the worst scenario, which was for me to not be able to play at all," he added, echoing the sentiment Roberts had repeatedly offered. "I'm confident that my overall performance should be better moving forward."

While both Ohtani and his manager indicated that he's still dealing with left knee, right biceps and neck discomfort — and he has been out of the lineup for two more games since Monday, making it six of the team's past seven — Roberts expressed hope that removing pitching from the equation will increase the chances that Ohtani the hitter remains available and impactful.

"That's part of the thought, to sort of take the pitching off of his plate and really try to let him lock in on being a hitter and get on track," Roberts said. "Because the last couple of weeks, he just hasn't been himself in the box."

With that brief and long-awaited media session, the saga of Ohtani's disjointed effort to resume his two-way heroics received a much-needed dose of clarity and, in a way, closure. The will-he-or-won't-he pitching inquiries can, it seems, be postponed until 2027. At that point, we can restore the pent-up excitement about seeing him back on the bump, and we should contemplate the broader viability of Ohtani remaining a two-way player for the entirety of his Dodgers contract, which stretches through the 2033 season.

But for now, Ohtani's acceptance of his various ailments and the increasingly high-stakes state of affairs with October fast approaching raises an entirely new series of questions involving his season and the Dodgers' push for a third consecutive championship. Can he battle through his injuries to rediscover his elite hitting form in time for the postseason? If his struggles continue, will Roberts consider moving him out of the leadoff spot for the first time this season? Will Ohtani's absence in the rotation be felt, or will the healthy aces step up as hoped? What if he reinjures his knee more seriously? Or, if he's feeling good — and sorry, we have to ask — will Ohtani try to make a miraculous push to be available on the mound for an inning late in October? And on and on.

How will Ohtani answer those questions in the coming weeks?

As has always been the case with him, we'll all be waiting and watching to find out.

articles.title: Ohio Sports Hall of Fame 2026 class honors Greater Cincinnati athletes
articles.summary: These Greater Cincinnati connections were selected to the Ohio Sports Hall of Fame class of 2026.
articles.body:
The Ohio Sports Hall of Fame has selected its 2026 class.

Established in 2024, the Hall's mission is to honor Ohio's greatest sports legends. The most recent class contained scores of athletes, coaches and administrators with Cincinnati ties.

The second annual induction banquet will be Saturday, Oct. 27, at the Dayton Convention Center. There will be dinner and a group photo at 5 p.m., with the ceremony running from 6:30 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. Tickets are available for purchase on the Ohio Sports Hall of Fame website .

These are the Greater Cincinnati connections who made it into the Ohio Sports Hall of Fame in 2026:

Mike Bobinski: Xavier University, Akron University, Purdue University athletic director

Brian Akers: Cincinnati CoBALTS semi-pro baseball player

Burke Badenhop : Cincinnati Reds pitcher

Keith Becker: Cincinnati CoBALTS semi-pro baseball player

Buddy Bell: Moeller High School player, Cincinnati Reds player and vice president

Ian Happ: University of Cincinnati, Chicago Cubs left fielder

Vince Harrison Jr.: Princeton High School and University of Kentucky player, minor league coach

Mike Hatfield: Cincinnati CoBALTS semi-pro baseball

Dummy Hoy: Deaf Cincinnati Reds center fielder
